id: Marjaa: The Battle of the Hotels
blurb: A haunting meditation on place and loss — field recordings and drones tracing Beirut's war-scarred landscape.
description: Swedish producer Civilistjävel (Tomas Bodén) takes Lebanese singer Mayssa Jallad's concept album about the 1975 Beirut civil war hotel battles and rebuilds it using dub techniques and minimal electronica, dissolving her Arabic vocals into something spare and heavy.

blurb: Slow, immersive ambient textures from Russia — vast and quietly unsettling.
description: Serwed is a duo from Saint Petersburg that makes ambient and post-club electronic music sitting somewhere between downtempo, digital dub, and musique concrète. Their V album leans into that slow, layered side.

blurb: Fragile electronic pop from Voice Actor — intimate, glitchy, and deeply strange.
description: Voice Actor's Noa Kurzweil teams up with Welsh producer Squu for a woozy, intimate set of ambient dub and soft electronic textures, Kurzweil's hushed vocals drifting over hazy pads and slow dubby pulses.

blurb: Congolese polyphonic voices woven through electronic production — joyful, hypnotic, and utterly singular.
description: French producer Rrobin travelled to Brazzaville in 2019 to record with the Mamans du Congo, a Congolese collective known for singing ancestral Kongo lullabies using everyday objects as instruments. The result mixes those vocals with electronic beats and rhythms, released in 2020.

blurb: Essential Cameroonian dance music from 1976–84 — electrifying highlife-infused funk curated by Analog Africa.
description: Analog Africa compilation from 2017 collecting Cameroonian funk and disco from 1976 to 1984, the period when local makossa style got plugged into synthesizers, electric guitars and the groove of West African nightclubs.

blurb: A solo piano masterpiece from Sapporo — Fukui's meditative, deeply personal approach to jazz standards.
description: Debut album from self-taught Sapporo pianist Ryo Fukui, recorded in 1976. It's mostly jazz standards played with a trio, sitting somewhere between modal jazz, bop, and cool jazz.

blurb: Ryo Fukui at his most lyrical — gentle and searching, recorded live in Sapporo in 1977.
description: Ryo Fukui's second album from 1977, a follow-up to Scenery with the same Sapporo trio. It covers similar post-bop ground but gets slightly more contemplative, with nods to Bill Evans alongside McCoy Tyner-style intensity.

blurb: The definitive trip-hop mix — Vienna's Kruder & Dorfmeister blend downtempo, dub, and groove into something timeless.
description: Vienna duo Kruder & Dorfmeister put together this 1996 mix for the DJ-Kicks series, blending trip-hop, jungle, acid jazz and downtempo. It's widely considered one of the best in the series and is still a benchmark for 90s European downtempo mixing.

blurb: Raw Detroit ghettotech from HiTech — bass-heavy, relentless, and deeply weird.
description: Detroit trio HiTech (King Milo, Milf Melly, and 47Chops) make ghettotech, the Motor City genre mixing ghetto house, techno and hip-hop. This 2025 mixtape is laser-focused on the dancefloor, with hyperspeed rhythms and call-and-response rapping.

blurb: Robert Henke's debut as Monolake — minimal dub techno built from the textures and spaces of Hong Kong.
description: Berlin duo Monolake (Robert Henke and Gerhard Behles) released this dub techno classic on Chain Reaction in 1997, built partly from field recordings they made during a trip to Hong Kong for a computer music conference. One of the foundational dub techno records.

blurb: Stephen Wilkinson's early home recordings — folk guitar and 8-track tape warmth, full of nostalgia and texture.
description: A short EP from Bibio (Stephen Wilkinson) released on Warp in 2009, companion to his Vignetting the Compost album. It has the same analogue lo-fi quality, dusty string samples, and skewed folk-electronic feel he's known for.

blurb: Cut-up recordings woven into delicate audio collage — The Books at their most tender and strange.
description: Second album from New York duo The Books, released in 2003. They layer acoustic instruments, string arrangements and found-sound samples into fragmented songs that sit between folk, ambient and musique concrète.

blurb: James Brown in raw, late-period form — rough-edged funk pushed to its limits.
description: James Brown's 1988 album, produced entirely by the NYC group Full Force. It brings new jack swing production to Brown's funk, a late-career record that sounds different from his 70s peak but still has Maceo Parker on saxophone.

blurb: Globetrotting trip-hop from Washington DC — lounge, dub, and bossa nova wrapped in sleek electronics.
description: Second album from Washington DC duo Thievery Corporation, released in 2000. It's trip-hop and downtempo with bossa nova, dub and lounge influences, featuring vocalists including Bebel Gilberto, and became their best-selling US record.

blurb: Early Fela — the seeds of afrobeat before the political fire fully ignited, recorded in Lagos in the late 1960s.
description: Early Fela Kuti recordings compiled across two volumes, capturing him before afrobeat fully crystallised. The music draws more on highlife and jazz, showing where he started before becoming the sound he became famous for.

id: Fela Ransome Kuti & His Koola Lobitos
artist: Fela Ransome Kuti & His Koola Lobitos
blurb: Fela's earliest recordings, blending highlife and jazz before afrobeat was born.
description: Pre-afrobeat recordings from Fela Kuti's mid-60s Lagos band, originally released as Nigerian 7-inch singles. The music blends highlife, jazz and soul, and features Fela primarily on trumpet rather than saxophone.

blurb: Egyptian pop and funk rarities curated by Habibi Funk — a forgotten chapter of Cairo's golden age.
description: Egyptian band Al Massrieen made one of the most distinctive records to come out of Cairo in the 80s, mixing disco, funk, boogie and jazz with synths and Arabic lyrics. This Habibi Funk reissue brings their 1984 album to a wider audience.

blurb: The Art of Noise at their most expansive — sampling and synthesis pushing pop's outer edges in 1986.
description: Second Art of Noise album, from 1986, the first they made after leaving ZTT Records. It's more song-structured than their debut, blending experimental synth-pop with orchestral touches, and produced their biggest UK hits including a cover of Peter Gunn with Duane Eddy.

blurb: Strange, playful, and avant-garde — The Art of Noise deconstructing pop with wit and orchestral chaos.
description: Third Art of Noise album, 1987, with the group now down to just Anne Dudley and JJ Jeczalik. It's dense and collage-like, mixing funky beats with orchestral pieces, field recordings and snatches of dialogue.

blurb: Dense, emotive drum and bass from Hong Kong — Gyrofield building cathedrals from bass and rhythm.
description: Debut EP from gyrofield, a Hong Kong-born, Bristol-based producer, released on XL Recordings in 2024. Four tracks of drum and bass and jungle, ranging from cerebral neurofunk to more spacious, atmospheric pieces.

blurb: Jamaican dub meets breakbeat — dubplate culture colliding with UK rave aesthetics.
description: Dub Specialists were a UK group connected to the Conscious Sounds label, and this record crosses dub basslines and reggae rhythms with funk samples and breakbeats, made using an Atari and a Soundcraft mixer in the 90s.

blurb: Fractured, intimate post-rock from Glasgow — Still House Plants making something new from jazz and indie.
description: Second album from Glasgow and South London trio Still House Plants, released in 2020. It was assembled from phone recordings, rehearsal tapes and live show captures, resulting in a fractured, lo-fi mix of experimental rock and jazz-influenced grooves.

blurb: Lee Perry's late-career meditation — spiritual, unhurried, and strangely beautiful.
description: Lee Scratch Perry's 2019 album, named after his birth name, made with producer Adrian Sherwood. Nine original tracks keeping the dub atmosphere he pioneered in the 70s, widely considered one of his best late-career records.

blurb: Acid house and techno from Richard D. James's early years — raw and hypnotic.
description: An unauthorised 1994 compilation of early Aphex Twin material, collecting the Digeridoo and Xylem Tube EPs plus a few extras. Richard D. James was reportedly unhappy about the release, but the tracks, heavy on acid and analogue synthesis, are genuinely essential.

blurb: Fractured pop from Airick Woodhead — dissonant, maximalist, and deeply anxious.
description: 2012 debut EP from Doldrums, the Montreal project of Airick Woodhead. It's glitchy, DIY electronic pop with noisy textures and hypnotic, somewhat chaotic energy, released on Arbutus Records alongside early peers like Grimes.

blurb: A dub landmark — King Tubby and Augustus Pablo creating one of the genre's defining works together.
description: 1976 dub classic produced by Augustus Pablo, recorded at Randy's studio in Kingston with the Barrett brothers on drums and bass, then mixed by King Tubby. Often listed among the greatest reggae albums ever made.

blurb: Late-career Aphex Twin — abstract, melancholy, and endlessly detailed.
description: A 2023 EP from Aphex Twin (Richard D. James), his first release under that name since 2018. It moves between tight, claustrophobic IDM percussion and more spacious ambient passages.

blurb: Warp's genre-defining 1992 compilation — the record that named intelligent dance music.
description: The 1992 Warp Records compilation that effectively named and launched IDM as a genre. Features early tracks from Aphex Twin, Autechre, The Black Dog, Speedy J and others, intended for sitting and listening rather than dancing.

blurb: A nocturnal Tokyo dispatch — jazz, electronics, and downtown cool from Studio Mule.
description: A 2018 compilation compiled by record store Ondas, bringing together obscure Japanese electric jazz, boogie, funk and soul from the 80s. Features contributions arranged by Ryuichi Sakamoto alongside lesser-known jazz fusion and electronic tracks.

blurb: Essential dub and reggae cuts from Jamaica's sound system generation.
description: A compilation of Jamaican dub and reggae cuts, drawing from the sound system generation and featuring artists like Lee Scratch Perry, U Roy and Eek-A-Mouse. A good sampler of foundational Jamaican dub and roots reggae.

blurb: Rare Malian recordings — the deep intersection of griot tradition and West African funk.
description: Compiled by Mr Bongo and Ostinato Records, this 2017 double LP collects Malian music from the 70s and 80s, including Sory Bamba, Salif Keita, Rail Band and Mory Kanté. Comes with a 24-page booklet on the country's music history.

blurb: Analog Africa's survey of Edo state funk — hypnotic rhythms from southern Nigeria, largely unheard until now.
description: Analog Africa's 2021 compilation focused on funk from Benin City in southern Nigeria, where musicians in the late 70s started mixing traditional Edo elements with disco, funk and reggae. Features Sir Victor Uwaifo, Osayomore Joseph and Akaba Man.

blurb: Mr. Bongo's eclectic global dig — funk, soul, and world music gathered from every corner of the globe.
description: Fifth instalment in the Mr Bongo curation series, released in 2022 as a double LP. It pulls from Brazil, Cuba, Ghana, Jamaica, Japan, Mauritania and beyond, spanning funk, soul, world music and disco from the 70s to the present.

blurb: Shakuhachi jazz from Japan — Muraoka's bamboo flute bridging ancient tradition and modern improvisation.
description: A 1970 album by Japanese shakuhachi player Minoru Muraoka, mixing traditional Japanese instruments with jazz arrangements and Western pop covers. Became a crate-digger favourite and has been sampled by Madlib, DJ Shadow and others.

blurb: One of Fela's most politically charged albums — a direct account of police persecution set to blazing afrobeat.
description: Two-track 1975 Fela Kuti album, each side a single long Afrobeat groove with Africa 70. The title comes from a real incident where Nigerian police planted a joint on Fela and detained him waiting for a stool sample he managed to fake.

blurb: Seminal Berlin dub techno — Basic Channel's hypnotic, minimal machine music from the early 90s.
description: Moritz von Oswald and Mark Ernestus recorded as Basic Channel in Berlin from 1993, and Inversion is one of their key early 12-inch releases. Their minimal, dubby techno gave rise to the term dub techno.

blurb: Lo-fi dub techno from Australia — hazy, distorted, and strangely moving.
description: Melbourne producer Tarquin Manek (M. Quake) collaborates with Jonnine from HTRK on this 2024 12-inch, reworking Annie Lennox's Little Bird into a slow, dubby piece built around a rubbery bassline and Jonnine's drawn-out vocals.

blurb: Enigma's ambient new age signature — Gregorian chant laid over electronic textures.
description: Enigma is the project of German-Romanian producer Michael Cretu, and this 1990 debut album mixed Gregorian chant samples with electronic beats and new age atmosphere. It sold over 15 million copies worldwide.

artist: Lee Scratch Perry and Mad Professor
blurb: Two legends of dub production in collaboration — deep, spiritual, and endlessly layered.
description: Lee Scratch Perry and Adrian Sherwood collaborator Mad Professor made this together in 1989, recording at Mad Professor's Ariwa studio in London. Digital drum machines and dub effects sit alongside Perry's characteristic stream-of-consciousness vocals.

blurb: Afro-Venezuelan folk traditions sung with raw power and ceremony by Luzmira Zerpa.
description: Luzmira Zerpa is a Venezuelan singer based in the UK, known for mixing Afro-Venezuelan folk traditions with contemporary sounds. Bocón features her over traditional coastal rhythms and polyrhythmic quitiplás percussion.

blurb: A tribute to Zanzibar's cultural heritage — taarab music and East African tradition.
description: Gibraltar Drakus was a member of Cameroonian group Les Têtes Brûlées, and this 1989 debut album was dedicated to their late guitarist Zanzibar Epeme. It's bikutsi music, a Cameroonian style driven by interlocking guitar and complex cross-rhythms.

id: I Haven't Got Anything Better to Do
blurb: Astrud Gilberto at her most intimate — bossa nova melancholy drifting over gentle jazz arrangements.
description: A 1969 Verve Records album from Brazilian bossa nova singer Astrud Gilberto, recorded in New York. It's a quiet, intimate set, closer to baroque pop and easy listening than her earlier samba recordings, built around late-night ballads.

blurb: Ali Love and Judge Jules's dub-inflected house anthem — warm, propulsive, and timeless.
description: The Mighty Dub Kats is a project from UK producer Norman Cook (later Fatboy Slim), and Magic Carpet Ride was a 1995 club single that hit the top 10 across Europe. It samples Cuban and soul records over a bouncy house groove.

blurb: Vieux Farka Touré's tribute to his legendary father — desert blues that transcends generations.
description: A 2022 album where Vieux Farka Touré, the Malian guitarist and son of Ali Farka Touré, recorded versions of his late father's songs in collaboration with Houston trio Khruangbin. The desert blues guitar style stays intact while the arrangements get a subtle psychedelic lean.

blurb: Afro-house and tribal rhythms filtered through the UK underground — roots and future colliding.
description: A 2001 UK 12-inch on Chillifunk Records, Afrix featuring Dorothee Ningabire's vocals on a tribal house cut that mixes African percussion with jazzy garage house grooves.

blurb: São Paulo's Sessa making meditative bossa nova for a new generation — slow-burning and gorgeous.
description: Second album from São Paulo musician Sessa, released in 2022. He sings in Portuguese over a bare, minimal take on bossa nova and tropicália, the arrangements stripped back compared to the lushness of his peers.

blurb: Analog Africa's excavation of a Guinean voice — luminous afrobeat with Cuban and jazz inflections.
description: Analog Africa compiled all ten tracks Amara Touré ever released, from his time in Cameroon and then Gabon between 1973 and 1980. Touré was Guinean and his music mixed West African mandingue sounds with Cuban-inflected brass and rhythm.

blurb: Habibi Funk's eclectic selection of Arabic music — spanning Egypt, Lebanon, Libya, and beyond.
description: A 2017 compilation from the Habibi Funk label collecting Arabic funk, soul, disco and pop from Morocco, Algeria, Egypt and Sudan, mostly from the late 70s and 80s. Features Fadoul, Al Massrieen, Attarazat Addahabia and others.

blurb: Sadao Watanabe's fusion of Japanese jazz and soul — lyrical saxophone over warmly produced grooves.
description: Japanese alto saxophonist Sadao Watanabe's 1979 jazz fusion album, recorded with a New York session band including Steve Gadd on drums and Dave Grusin on piano. It sits in the smooth, funk-edged jazz fusion style of that era.

blurb: Early Azymüth demos revealing the roots of samba-funk fusion — spontaneous and deeply alive.
description: Previously unheard home studio recordings by Brazilian jazz-funk trio Azymuth, made in Rio de Janeiro before their 1975 debut album. Their signature samba doido sound is already in place, mixing electric jazz, psychedelia and Brazilian rhythm.

blurb: Turkish deep house with Mediterranean warmth — Mutlu San building subtle, aquatic grooves.
description: Istanbul-based producer Mutlu San's 2018 EP on Lessizmore Records, four tracks of minimal deep house and micro-techno with careful sound design that moves between driving and meditative.

blurb: A survey of Nigeria's most explosive dance music — afrobeat performers at their peak.
description: A Nigerian afrobeat and funk compilation pulling from the 70s Lagos scene, featuring artists who followed in the wake of Fela Kuti and mixed highlife, funk, soul and brass into the Afrobeat style.

blurb: Fela's anti-military opus — a relentless critique of Nigeria's army delivered as unstoppable funk.
description: Fela Kuti's 1976 album, two long tracks using the zombie metaphor to attack the Nigerian military. It triggered a brutal retaliatory raid by Nigerian soldiers on his Kalakuta Republic commune, during which his mother was fatally injured.

id: The Very Best of Billy Boyo
blurb: Billy Boyo's dancehall toasting at its finest — wit and rhythm from Jamaica's golden era.
description: Billy Boyo (1971-2000) was one of Jamaica's most prolific child DJs, recording toasting vocals over roots reggae riddims in the early 80s. He's best known for One Spliff a Day and has been sampled by The Avalanches.

blurb: Fela dissects gender roles with wit and fury — two long afrobeat workouts at full power.
description: A 1972 Fela Kuti album with Africa 70, two long tracks blending jazz, highlife and maturing afrobeat. Lady attacks Western-influenced African women and Shakara mocks the boastful, both in Broken English accessible across Anglophone Africa.

id: But You Caint Use My Phone
blurb: Erykah Badu's mixtape moment — neo-soul layered over interpolations of classic R&B, raw and free.
description: Erykah Badu's 2015 mixtape, recorded in eleven days with Dallas producer Zach Witness. She called it TRap & B, a mixture of trap-influenced beats and her jazz and R&B instincts, with an André 3000 appearance.

blurb: Badu's sprawling second album — longer, stranger, and more jazz-inflected than anything before.
description: Erykah Badu's second album from 2000, recorded at Electric Lady Studios in New York with the Soulquarians collective, Questlove, Pino Palladino and Jay Dee among them. It's live-instrument neo soul with Bag Lady as its biggest single.

blurb: Erykah Badu's debut — neo-soul as spiritual practice, every track a ceremony.
description: Erykah Badu's 1997 debut, and one of the defining neo soul records. Her voice is unlike anyone else, and the whole album feels warm, slow-burning, and deeply felt.

blurb: Compact and confidently weird — Badu's 2003 return rewrote neo-soul's vocabulary in under 40 minutes.
description: Erykah Badu's 2003 EP-length release, more experimental and stripped back than her earlier work, mixing neo soul with jazz and spoken word in a tight, focused set.

blurb: Archie Marshall's debut full-length — a grey London howl soaked in jazz, punk, and dub.
description: King Krule's 2013 debut full-length, combining post-punk guitars, jazz, and gritty south London atmosphere with Archy Marshall's distinctive deep, ragged vocals.

blurb: King Krule's sprawling 2023 double album — looser, more intimate, and deeply felt.
description: A short, raw EP from King Krule released in 2016, mostly just his voice and guitar, intimate and lo-fi in a way that suits the bleakness of the songs.

blurb: D'Angelo's fifteen-year comeback — a restless, politically charged neo-soul masterpiece.
description: D'Angelo's return after 14 years away, released in 2014. It's dense, funky, and complex, layering live band performances and soul with political urgency.

blurb: Berlin-based Jemba Groove channeling African rhythm and soul into something warm and original.
description: Debut album from Jembaa Groove, a Berlin-based seven-piece founded by a German producer and a Ghanaian vocalist. They blend West African highlife and traditional sounds from Ghana and Mali with 70s soul and Berlin jazz, released in 2022.

blurb: Dense German dub-jungle fusion — layers of bass and rhythm colliding in controlled chaos.
description: A late-90s UK release from The Dub Funk Association, a collective pulling together producers from England, the Netherlands, and Australia. The album mixes dub, jungle, and reggae into heavy, textured tracks.

id: Nairobi Matata Jazz - Mapenzi Hayana Daktari
blurb: Rare Kenyan jazz — a Nairobi snapshot from the golden era of East African music.
description: Nairobi Matata Jazz were a band of Kenyan and Congolese musicians who played at Club Vibro in Nairobi. This track, edited by Frankie Francis, is a joyful slice of East African 70s dance music.

blurb: Darkly melodic alt-rock from The Crying Nudes — angular and emotionally raw.
description: An enigmatic UK alternative release associated with Dean Blunt's World Music label. Short, abrupt indie rock songs from a band that has kept its identity deliberately obscure.

blurb: Hard UK jungle with raw energy — Stekker's fierce club music.
description: Stekker is a Netherlands-based producer who makes old-school jungle using Commodore Amiga, Atari ST, and Akai samplers. This 2025 track pitches propulsive breakbeats against swirling ambient synths.

blurb: Neapolitan disco-funk from Nu Genea — Naples's sound refracted through a warm Mediterranean haze.
description: Nu Genea are a duo from Naples, and this 2022 album is built around the idea of the Mediterranean as a meeting point of cultures. It moves between Neapolitan folk, Afrobeat, jazz-funk, and Italo-disco.

blurb: Coltrane's Blue Note masterpiece — hard bop at its most urgent and focused.
description: John Coltrane's 1957 Blue Note album, and the only one he made for the label as a leader. It features a strong quintet including Lee Morgan and Curtis Fuller, playing hard bop at its most direct.

blurb: Industrial breakbeat from Germany — fierce, dark, and relentless.
description: Palm Skin Productions is British producer Simon Richmond, whose early releases landed on Mo' Wax. This 1996 record combines trip-hop, jazz, and big beat with a raw, bass-heavy edge.

blurb: South African township music with electrifying energy — Sandy B's mbaqanga-infused dance.
description: Sandy B is a kwaito pioneer from Durban who originally self-released this on cassette in 1994. It mixes Chicago and NYC house with West Coast hip-hop and Zulu rapping, running at a loose 100bpm.

blurb: A snapshot of early 90s trance and progressive house — euphoric, hypnotic, and formative.
description: A compilation drawing from the early trance and progressive house scene, featuring tracks that move between euphoric builds, hypnotic rhythms, and extended mixes built for the dancefloor.

blurb: Classic Jamaican deejay toasting — Trinity's rapid-fire delivery over roots rhythms.
description: Trinity was a Jamaican DJ and toaster known for his sharp, fast-paced delivery. This 1977 album is classic roots reggae, packed with his witty and confident vocal style over heavy rhythms.

blurb: Monk live at the Five Spot — angular, playful piano over one of jazz's most distinctive rhythm sections.
description: A live recording of Thelonious Monk's quartet from the Five Spot in New York in 1958, with John Coltrane on tenor saxophone. Loose, spontaneous, and one of the great jazz live albums.

blurb: The organ groove that launched a thousand samples — Booker T.'s landmark soul-jazz instrumental.
description: Booker T. and the MGs' 1962 debut, built around the organ-driven groove of the title track. It's instrumental soul and R&B at its most direct, and it defined the Stax Records sound.

id: Pepe, Bod and Dirt - RinkyDink EP
blurb: French funk and breakbeat from the 90s underground — rough, eclectic, and inventive.
description: A 1998 collaboration involving French house producer Pépé Bradock alongside Bod and Dirt. The EP mixes deep funk, breakbeat, and electronic grooves in the style of the late-90s French scene.

blurb: San Francisco's Dubtribe Sound System blending dub, tribal house, and deep electronic rhythms.
description: Dubtribe Sound System were a San Francisco duo who made tribal, dub-influenced house through the 90s and early 2000s. This 2003 album is more personal and introspective than their earlier work.

blurb: Mid-90s UK deep house at its most contemplative — subtle, melancholy, and beautifully constructed.
description: A 2000 release from Nightsource, the project of San Francisco producers Miguel Migs and Rasoul, on the Naked Music label. It moves between smooth deep house and downtempo trip-hop.

blurb: Congo's broadcasting orchestra — Brazzaville rumba and soukous from the golden age of state radio.
description: A 1983 album from one of Congo-Brazzaville's most celebrated orchestras. The band played a polished mix of Congolese rumba and soukous with big horn arrangements and strong vocal performances.

blurb: Nitin Sawhney's genre-defying fusion of Indian classical, flamenco, and electronic production.
description: Nitin Sawhney's 1996 debut on Outcaste Records, mixing south Asian classical music and percussion with trip-hop beats, flamenco, and jazz. It was an early landmark of the British Asian Underground.

blurb: Lahore quartet Jaubi merging Pakistani classical music with modern jazz — meditative and profound.
description: Debut album from Jaubi, a jazz quartet from Lahore, Pakistan, released in 2021. It draws on North Indian classical music and modal jazz, recorded with collaborators from London and Poland.

blurb: Mexican electronic producer Wakal channeling cumbia, house, and street sounds into sharp, danceable music.
description: Wakal is the project of Mexico City producer Jorge Govea, and this 2003 album layers field recordings of street vendors, mariachi, and city sounds over house, trip-hop, and downtempo rhythms.

blurb: Luke Vibert's classic drum and bass material — frenetic, playful, and technically dazzling.
description: Plug is one of the aliases of British producer Luke Vibert, and this 2012 release collects unreleased drum and bass tracks he made between 1995 and 1998, found on old DAT tapes.

blurb: Cornish folk sung in the Cornish language — intimate, ancient, and utterly beautiful.
description: Debut album from Cornish musician Daisy Rickman, released in 2022. Several songs are in the Cornish language, and the album is acoustic folk, mostly just her voice and guitar, self-recorded at home.

blurb: A meditative journey blending South Asian classical traditions with ambient electronic textures.
description: London-based painter and musician Jatinder Singh Durhailay is trained in Indian classical music and plays rare instruments including the dilruba and taus. This 2019 album combines those traditions with ambient and avant-garde composition.

blurb: Talvin Singh's Mercury Prize-winning debut — tabla meets drum and bass in a London-Indian fusion.
description: Talvin Singh's 1998 debut on Island Records won the Mercury Prize in 1999. He blends tabla and Indian classical music with drum and bass and jungle, recording in London, India, and Okinawa.

blurb: Mark Van Hoen's 1997 ambient record — melancholic, cinematic, and quietly devastating.
description: Locust is the alias of British electronic musician Mark Van Hoen, and this 1997 Apollo album mixes fractured IDM beats, ambient electronics, and trip-hop with live instruments and vocals from Neil Halstead of Slowdive.

blurb: Music from Memory's ambient meditation — slow, luminous, deeply immersive.
description: Courtney Bailey is a Tokyo-born, Berlin-based DJ and producer, and this 2025 debut album moves between ambient, new age, and dancefloor electronics, with soft spoken vocals drawing on her Japanese background.

blurb: Joanne Robertson's quietly devastating debut — sparse guitar and a haunting voice.
description: Joanne Robertson is a Blackpool-raised singer and guitarist who releases on Dean Blunt's World Music label. This 2023 album is eleven acoustic guitar and voice recordings spanning roughly a decade, intimate and diary-like.

blurb: Guadeloupean gwo ka and zouk-funk hybrid — rare Caribbean music full of heat and ceremony.
description: Erick Cosaque was a key figure in Guadeloupean music, rooted in the island's gwo-ka percussion tradition. This 1977 album, reissued in 2021, mixes that tradition with funky bass, horns, and expressive vocals.

blurb: Panjabi MC's bhangra-electronic fusion — the dhol beat that crossed continents.
description: Panjabi MC is a UK producer who brought bhangra into contact with hip-hop, jungle, garage, and ragga. This 2001 album moves across those styles, with the title track featuring dhol drums and Master Saleem on vocals.

blurb: Felix Manuel's genre-defying ambient-electronic record — layered, patient, deeply atmospheric.
description: Felix Manuel, who records as Djrum, released this in 2025 after a six-year gap following a hard drive failure that destroyed his original work. The album spans ambient, drum and bass, and broken beat, with significant live instrumentation including harp, piano, and cello.

blurb: Speedy J's debut on Warp — fast, hard techno from Rotterdam with an industrial edge.
description: Jochem Paap, a Dutch producer recording as Speedy J, released this debut album on Warp in 1993 as part of their Artificial Intelligence series. It roots itself in Detroit techno but pulls toward ambient and IDM.

blurb: Japanese electronic music at its most abstract — sora building intricate, fragile sonic architectures.
description: Sora is Kyoto producer Takeshi Kurosawa, who discovered electronic music via Warp Records after a classical piano upbringing. This 2003 album is minimal and drifting, mixing electronica with glitch, bossa nova, and jazz references.

blurb: Mercury Prize-winning drum and bass — Roni Size and Reprazent redefining the genre with jazz and soul.
description: Roni Size and the Bristol collective Reprazent won the 1997 Mercury Prize with this debut. It's drum and bass built from hip-hop, funk, and soul, with live bass and drums giving it a different feel from most electronic music of the time.

blurb: FSOL's double-album ambient masterpiece — sprawling, alien, and endlessly detailed.
description: The Future Sound of London's 1994 double album on Virgin, featuring Elizabeth Fraser and Robert Fripp as guests. It moved away from their earlier rave music toward dense, layered ambient techno and IDM.

blurb: Indian Vibes' Mathar reimagined by artists across the globe — bhangra and electronic music colliding.
description: Indian Vibes were a UK group, and this 1994 single and its remixes blend Indian classical elements with jazz-funk and house. Paul Weller played guitar and sitar, and remixes were contributed by Brendan Lynch and Primal Scream.

blurb: Sahel Sounds' remarkable document — music shared across the Sahara via mobile phones.
description: A 2022 Sahel Sounds compilation collecting recordings that musicians from across the Sahel sent over WhatsApp during the pandemic lockdown of 2020. The music ranges from Tuareg guitar to Mauritanian synth to Nigerien techno.

blurb: Guillermo Scott Herren's dense, hip-hop-influenced electronica — a watershed moment in glitch music.
description: Prefuse 73 is Atlanta-raised producer Scott Herren, and this 2001 Warp debut built his name on micro-sampled, glitchy hip-hop instrumentals. It features MF Doom, Aesop Rock, and other MC collaborators throughout.

blurb: The voice of the Sahrawi people — Mariem Hassan singing the pain and pride of Western Sahara.
description: Mariem Hassan was a Sahrawi singer who grew up in refugee camps in Algeria and sang in Hassaniya Arabic. This 2012 album was inspired by the Arab Spring and the Sahrawi independence movement, mixing traditional haul music with blues and jazz inflections.

blurb: Keigo Oyamada's pop maximalism — a dizzyingly eclectic sonic collage from 1990s Tokyo.
description: Cornelius is the alias of Tokyo musician Keigo Oyamada, and this 1997 album is a key record of the Shibuya-kei movement. It jumps between indie pop, electronic, cartoon-like sound collages, and shoegaze in a deliberately playful way.

blurb: Art of Noise reimagining Debussy through sampling and orchestration — a bold conceptual statement.
description: Art of Noise's final album, released in 1999, with Trevor Horn, Anne Dudley, and Paul Morley taking Debussy's work as a starting point. John Hurt narrates passages about the composer's life between tracks.

blurb: Dorothy Ashby's masterwork — jazz harp melodies inspired by Persian poetry, with lush orchestration.
description: Dorothy Ashby was a jazz harpist from Detroit who also played koto, and this 1970 Cadet album draws on the Persian poetry of Omar Khayyam. She wrote every track, sings and speaks throughout, and the orchestration gives it a Chicago soul-jazz feel.

blurb: The original Saharan cellphone collection — lo-fi recordings from Niger's Tuareg music scene.
description: A 2010 Sahel Sounds compilation assembled from MP3s traded on cellphones in northern Mali and the Sahara, collected by label founder Christopher Kirkley by swapping files with people he met in the street. It covers Tuareg guitar, autotune desert pop, Mauritanian synth, and Malian hip-hop.

blurb: Fairuz — the undimmed voice of Lebanon — at her most pure and emotionally devastating.
description: Fairuz is the most celebrated living Arab singer, and this 1987 album was produced by her son Ziad Rahbani, who brought jazz and funk orchestration to her voice. Recorded in Beirut in 1983 and 1984 and has become a touchstone of Arabic funk.

blurb: Niger's Les Filles de Illighadad — all-female Tuareg music rooted in ceremony and village life.
description: Les Filles de Illighadad are a Tuareg group from a small village in Niger, founded by Fatou Seidi Ghali, said to be the first Tuareg woman to play guitar professionally. The 2016 self-titled debut mixes acoustic guitar with tende, a traditional polyphonic percussion form.

blurb: A curated collection of Fairuz's most beloved recordings — the voice of Lebanon, spanning generations.
description: A compilation of Fairuz's contemporary recordings from the 70s to the 90s, mostly jazz-influenced tracks from her collaborations with son Ziad Rahbani. A good entry point to her later output.

blurb: Meditative ambient soundscapes that drift between texture and melody.
description: Colour Filter is the alias of Tokyo-based musician and nuclear physicist Ryuji Tsuneyoshi. This 2000 album makes gentle, melodic ambient pop and indietronica.

blurb: Hazy, cosmic electronics from Philadelphia's PLO Man — slow-moving and deeply hypnotic.
description: PLO Man is a Berlin-based DJ and producer and co-founder of the Acting Press label. This 2015 cassette release mixes ambient techno with atmospheric drum and bass in a long, immersive DJ mix format.

blurb: Daniel Maunick of Incognito explores Afro-Brazilian rhythms with deep funk and jazz sensibility.
description: Daniel Maunick is the son of Incognito's Bluey Maunick and grew up in London's drum and bass and broken beat scenes. This 2019 debut on Far Out Recordings moves between Afro-Brazilian percussion, deep house, broken beat, and jungle.

id: What It's Like to Be a Bat
blurb: A sonic exploration inspired by Thomas Nagel's philosophy essay.
description: Finn Streuper is a composer and producer from the Netherlands, and this 2026 debut takes its title from Thomas Nagel's philosophy paper on consciousness. It combines jazz, electronics, and library music in a weightless, atmospheric style.

blurb: Detroit's Stacey Pullen delivers a deep, hypnotic journey through underground techno and house for !K7's iconic DJ Kicks series.
description: Stacey Pullen is a Detroit techno DJ from the second wave of the scene, mentored by Derrick May and Kevin Saunderson. This 1996 DJ Kicks mix draws on Detroit techno and deep house with fast cuts and intricate blends.

blurb: A Detroit techno landmark — Kenny Larkin at his most precise and emotive, balancing machine rhythm with human feeling.
description: Kenny Larkin is a Detroit producer and this 1994 debut on Warp is a core record of the second wave of Detroit techno. It ranges from hard machine funk to ambient and soulful electronics.

blurb: A deep, rolling drum and bass record from Pressure — heavy sub bass and intricate rhythms.
description: Ability II is the alias of UK producer David Duncan, who recorded one EP in Leeds around 1991 that became a cult classic in the bleep and bass and early jungle world. The title track has a bassline so deep it gave mastering engineers trouble.

blurb: Italian library music at its most sublime — Torossi's lush, orchestral moods from the golden era of RAI production.
description: A 1974 Italian library music album recorded by Stefano Torossi and collaborators under pseudonyms due to contractual restrictions. It mixes cinematic funk, deep bass, strings, and breakbeats, and became a cult holy grail of the library music world.

blurb: JPEGMAFIA under his early alias — raw, lo-fi hip hop collaging video game sounds and political fury from Baltimore.
description: An early Devon Hendryx project from 2009, built from sample-based collage and lo-fi electronic production, with all tracks named after video games. Often cited as an accidental precursor to vaporwave.

blurb: An unlikely collaboration between Dean Blunt and Iceage's frontman — sparse, unsettling, and quietly brilliant.
description: A 2025 EP from UK artist Dean Blunt and Iceage vocalist Elias Rønnenfelt, produced with Vegyn. Sixteen minutes split into seven untitled pieces, mixing post-punk guitar and foggy indie rock with Rønnenfelt's deadpan singing.

blurb: Joni Mitchell's restless 1975 record — jazz arrangements, suburban critique, and songwriting at its most compositionally ambitious.
description: Joni Mitchell's 1975 album, her seventh, where she moves further from folk into jazz, adding African percussion samples, synthesizers, and the Jazz Crusaders. It was poorly received at the time but is now considered one of her best.

blurb: Air's warmest and most melodic record — French electronic pop drifting through weightless synths and hushed vocals.
description: The 2004 album by French duo Air, a return to the warm synth-pop and downtempo sound of their debut after a more rock-oriented detour. Clean, spacious, and melodic, it was one of their most commercially successful records.

blurb: LTJ Bukem's landmark 1995 full-length — intelligent drum and bass sculpted from jazz and ambient textures.
description: LTJ Bukem's long-awaited 2000 debut album on his own Good Looking Records label, blending drum and bass with jazz, soul, and ambient. It peaked at number 40 on the UK Albums Chart and is considered a defining record in the intelligent drum and bass style.

blurb: Soul Jazz Records' essential compilation of women who recorded for Studio One — heartfelt, powerful, and long overdue.
description: A 2005 Soul Jazz Records compilation collecting rare female vocals from Jamaica's legendary Studio One label, spanning ska, rocksteady, and early reggae. Features Marcia Griffiths, Hortense Ellis, Jennifer Lara, and others.

blurb: Bryn Jones's oblique tribute to Pakistan and Islam — dense, droning electronic music shot through with Middle Eastern samples.
description: A posthumous archival release from Muslimgauze, the project of British artist Bryn Jones who died in 1999. It draws on his signature style of South Asian-influenced percussion loops, field recordings, and minimal electronics.

blurb: Guadeloupean gwo ka rhythms fused with funk electricity — Erick Cosaque drawing Caribbean ceremonial music into new territory.
description: A 2019 compilation covering Guadeloupean percussionist and singer Erick Cosaque from 1973 to 1995, tracing his career mixing the Afro-Caribbean gwo-ka tradition with funk, jazz, and zouk.

blurb: Dublin ambient artist Ian Nyquist sculpting slow, luminous soundscapes — patient music that rewards deep listening.
description: A 2025 album by Dublin-based sound artist Ian Nyquist, built around innovative bodhrán playing combined with ambient textures and electronic production. He developed a new technique using modelling software to mirror his drumming gestures.

blurb: Marylou Mayniel's 2025 album as Oklou — glitchy, emotional PC music from Paris with an aching pop core.
description: The 2025 debut LP from French producer and vocalist Oklou (Marylou Mayniel), mixing dreamy electronic pop with trance, ambient, and Y2K-era influences. She is associated with the NUXXE collective, and the album features production from Danny L. Harle and A.G. Cook.

blurb: Meditative ambient electronics from Car Culture — unhurried, soft-edged, and quietly absorbing.
description: The 2025 sophomore album from Car Culture, the project of New Jersey-born Queens-based artist Daniel Fisher, released on Montreal's NAFF Recordings. It moves between downtempo, dream pop, and ambient, built over three years between New York and Montreal.

blurb: Aymara sibling duo blending Bolivian folk and Andean tradition with contemporary electronic production.
description: The 2025 self-titled debut from Los Thuthanaka, an American sibling duo of Aymara heritage, blending traditional Andean music like huayno and kullawada with experimental electronic production.

blurb: Korean musician Gu's warmly mysterious album — layered acoustic guitar, voice, and ambient texture that defies easy description.
description: A 2018 solo album by South Korean musician Mid-Air Thief, recorded in a basement apartment, fusing acoustic folk instrumentation with electronic production and Korean vocals. It built a cult following after being reissued on vinyl by Topshelf Records.

blurb: UK bass music with a Middle Eastern edge — Pocz & Pacheko building heavy, textured electronic music from unexpected sources.
description: A 2010 EP from Venezuelan duo Pocz and Pacheko on the UK label Senseless Records, mixing UK funky rhythms and deep dubstep sub-bass with Latin percussion influences.

blurb: Hey Colossus at their most ferocious — UK rock that refuses to sit still, dragging punk and noise into wild new shapes.
description: A nearly 22-minute cover by UK noise rock band Hey Colossus, reworking a Patrick Cowley and Jorge Socarras original into a sprawling psychedelic dub piece. Released as part of the state51 Singularity series in 2023.

blurb: UK electronic producer Lunch Money Life crafting deep, searching music at the intersection of soul and synthesis.
description: A 2023 single from London five-piece Lunch Money Life, featuring Lady Lykez and Suku Ward, built over a deep reggae-dub rhythm. Named one of The Quietus's best tracks of the year.

id: Look Over the Wall, See the Sky
blurb: Irish folk singer John Francis Flynn revisiting traditional songs with a quietly radical touch — deeply rooted and quietly strange.
description: The second album from Dublin folk artist John Francis Flynn, released on Rough Trade's River Lea imprint, reworking traditional Irish songs against a distorted urban soundscape.

blurb: Manila-born jungle and breakbeat music with Filipino soul — Ezzrei and Celeste Legaspi bridging two musical worlds.
description: A track by Manila-based DJ and producer Ezzrei, flipping the classic Filipino love song 'Ang Daigdig Ko'y Ikaw' as sung by Celeste Legaspi into a deep, dubby junglist edit. Ezzrei is the founder of CONTINUUM BASS, the Philippines' first bass music platform.

blurb: UK producer Saphy Vong's Neo Geodesia project blending Cambodian heritage with cutting-edge electronic production.
description: A 2026 album by Neo Geodesia (Saphy Vong), a Brighton-based producer of Cambodian heritage, merging traditional Khmer pinpeat and martial arts music with powerviolence and electronic production.

blurb: Egyptian singer Maryam Saleh exploring the avant-garde edges of Arabic song — theatrical, political, and beautifully strange.
description: A 2026 album by Egyptian singer and composer Maryam Saleh, her first in nearly eight years, co-produced with Maurice Louca. It draws on Egyptian song forms including mawwal, lullaby, and muwashshah, and the title means 'secret' in Arabic.

blurb: Analog Africa unearthing rare Central African recordings — rhythms from Gabon that the wider world nearly missed.
description: The opening track from a 2026 Analog Africa compilation gathering recordings by Antoine Dougbé and the Orchestre Poly-Rythmo de Cotonou from 1977 to 1982, made in Benin. The music mixes circular guitars, hypnotic synths, Afro-Cuban grooves, and Cavacha rhythms.

blurb: Melbourne's anonymous Indian-Australian trio crafting psychedelic raga-influenced music.
description: A 2024 EP from Melbourne trio Glass Beams on Ninja Tune, mixing Indian-influenced psychedelic funk with live instrumentation and DIY electronics. The band draws on the tradition of Indian artists like R.D. Burman and Ananda Shankar who fused Western and South Asian music.

blurb: DMZ founder Mala collaborating with South African artist Thebe Magugu — dub bass and bass weight meeting fashion and identity.
description: A 2024 single from UK dubstep pioneer Mala and Nigeria-born MC Magugu, released on Deep Medi Musik. Magugu raps in English-Nigerian Pidgin over Mala's tightly coiled bass production.

blurb: New Jersey's Wilhelmina building club-focused electronic music with personality and hypnotic groove.
description: A track from Wilhelmina's 'Book of Spells' project, a Philadelphia-based artist making club music that draws on jersey club, techno, and his Filipino heritage.

blurb: New York-based Grupo Candombe bridging Cuban son and Afro-Latin ceremony — joyful, percussive, and deeply cultural.
description: A track by Grupo Candombe, a Cuban-rooted Latin band, mixing Afro-Cuban rhythms with dance and funk influences.

blurb: Palestinian singer Saied Silbak keeping traditional Arabic song alive — a voice carrying the weight of memory and longing.
description: A 2025 album by London-based Palestinian composer and oud player Saied Silbak, featuring intimate trio arrangements of Palestinian folkloric songs alongside an original piece written in response to the war in Gaza.

blurb: Solo guitar improvisations from Tokyo — delicate fingerpicking and extended technique exploring the instrument's inner landscape.
description: A 1999 album by Osaka-based musician Daisuke Tobari, originally self-released on cassette, containing 22 untitled lo-fi acoustic folk tracks that shift between folk, drone, and tape experiments.

blurb: Named for the Spanish poet, Lorca sees Buckley abandon conventional song.
description: Tim Buckley's fifth album from 1970, named after the Spanish poet, where he largely abandons conventional songwriting in favour of freeform jazz and avant-garde experimentation. He uses his four-octave voice as an instrument rather than a vehicle for melody.

blurb: Czech singer-songwriter of rare emotional depth with intimate guitar and voice recordings.
description: A 1987 Czech folk album by self-taught guitarist and singer Dagmar Andrtová-Voňková, who uses unconventional guitar techniques including playing with a bow to push folk song into rawer, more transcendental territory. She emerged from the Czech underground folk scene.

blurb: Uruguayan singer-songwriter Jorge Lazaroff at his most poetic — gentle songs balancing tenderness with political consciousness.
description: A 1982 album by Uruguayan singer-songwriter Jorge Lazaroff, who worked in the nueva canción tradition and died in 1989 at 39. His music combines folk with a literary sensibility rooted in Montevideo.

blurb: Julian Koster's baroque folk odyssey — homemade instruments, carnival spirit, and a deep sense of wonder navigating imaginary symphonies.
description: The 1999 debut album from The Music Tapes, Julian Koster's project, recorded over four years using tape recorders and a wax cylinder recorder. Jeff Mangum of Neutral Milk Hotel contributed, and the sound sits between 1920s lo-fi pop and sound collage.

id: You Are My Everlovin / Celestial Power
blurb: American avant-garde iconoclast blending hillbilly fiddle, Appalachian drone, and conceptual art, making music that dissolves genres.
description: A 1986 album by American avant-garde artist Henry Flynt featuring two long-form drone pieces recorded in 1980 and 1981, using distorted electric violin and tape loops to synthesize Appalachian folk with Indian raga. Each side runs about 45 minutes.

blurb: Yorkshire singer-songwriter with a looping guitar and a voice that carries whole lifetimes.
description: The 2005 debut album by Yorkshire singer-songwriter David Thomas Broughton, recorded in a single continuous take at a church hall in Leeds, with bells audible in the background. He uses live sampling of his own guitar and voice to build layers during performance.

blurb: A cornerstone of Brazilian music — Nascimento's miraculous falsetto and spiritual intensity make this one of his most urgent records.
description: Milton Nascimento's 1973 album, where three of the original songs had their lyrics removed by Brazil's military censors rather than altered. Eight of the eleven tracks are instrumental as a result, making it one of the more unusual records in the MPB canon.

blurb: The Akvarium co-founder going deep into Russian folk and post-punk territory — a record of strange but meditative beauty.
description: An avant-folk album by Leonid Fedorov, frontman of the long-running St. Petersburg band Auktyon, blending live instrumentation with sampled Slavic folk material. It moves between distant, eerie textures and full folk ballads.

blurb: Maine family folk-rock — Caleb and Colleen Mulkerin making art-damaged music from domestic life.
description: A 2008 home-recorded album from Big Blood, the experimental folk project of Colleen Kinsella and Caleb Mulkerin based in South Portland, Maine. It ranges from tense gothic folk to cracked Americana, with roots in the New Weird America scene.

blurb: The most extreme of Buckley's departures, with his voice treated like a free jazz instrument over wordless soundscapes.
description: Tim Buckley's sixth album from 1970, his most avant-garde record, where he treats his voice as a free jazz instrument over loosely structured experimental backings. It contains 'Song to the Siren' and was ranked by Pitchfork among the best albums of the 1970s.

blurb: Greek rock singer Yannis Aggelakas exploring the space where protest poetry meets post-rock.
description: A 2005 double album by Giannis Aggelakas and his band Oi Episkeptes, spanning 24 songs and nearly two hours of Greek alternative folk. Aggelakas is known from the influential Greek rock band Trypes.

blurb: Hoarse-voiced Greek prophet Thanasis Papakonstantinou — songs rooted in laïká tradition.
description: A 2000 album by Greek singer-songwriter Thanasis Papakonstantinou from Larissa, blending traditional Greek folk song forms with rock and jazz. It was described as a turning point for rock-traditional fusion in Greece.

blurb: Yerevan's genre-defying collective mixing Armenian folk, jazz, and avant-garde — playful but deeply rooted in cultural memory.
description: The 2001 second album from the Armenian Navy Band, the project of Armenian-heritage percussionist Arto Tunçboyaciyan, recorded in Istanbul with a twelve-piece ensemble. It mixes traditional Armenian instruments like duduk and kemanche with jazz horns and contemporary playing.

blurb: Mexican singer La Bruja de Texcoco fusing petenera flamenco, son jarocho, and protest tradition into something fiercely her own.
description: A 2019 album from La Bruja de Texcoco, the project of Mexican artist Octavio Mendoza, blending son huasteco and other Mexican folk forms with personal, feminist perspectives. Five long tracks draw on traditional forms while rejecting the machismo often embedded in them.

blurb: Newcastle's bard conjures medieval England with oblique lyrics and raw guitar — Peasant is a folk album unlike anything folk has produced.
description: Richard Dawson's 2017 album, where each song is written from the perspective of a different person in a seventh-century Northumbrian community, including a soldier, weaver, prostitute, and beggar. The Newcastle singer-guitarist plays with a deliberately rough, eccentric sound mixing folk and avant-garde.

blurb: John Cale's production frames Nico's German baritone in orchestral grandeur — glacial, devotional, and deeply strange.
description: Nico's 1970 album, co-produced by John Cale, where she sings in German over chamber arrangements that reference Mahler and German song cycles. It is far from the Western pop tradition and includes 'Janitor of Lunacy', written in tribute to Brian Jones.

blurb: Czech prog-folk hidden gem — Mirek Kemel's late 70s recordings balancing acoustic introspection with orchestral ambition.
description: A 2000 album from Czech ensemble Rale, five musicians who sing in Czech, French, English, Polish, Vietnamese, Japanese, and Spanish, sometimes within the same song. Violin, cello, guitar, and hand percussion make up the instrumentation.

blurb: French experimental rock vocalist at her most radical — voices and organ merging into hypnotic, devotional peace.
description: Catherine Ribeiro and Alpes's 1972 album, considered their best, mixing folk, psychedelia, and progressive rock with Ribeiro's striking vocals and long, complex compositions. It was out of print for decades and had a cult following built partly through scarcity.

blurb: An epic outsider folk-punk cycle from the American underground — uncompromising, personal, and gloriously lo-fi.
description: A 2017 album from Chicago-based experimental artist Gypyrd Samuelson, built with electric kazoos, tape loops, and oddball production. It sits somewhere between outsider art and lo-fi indie rock.

artist: Opus Posth Ensemble / Dmitry Pokrovsky Folk Ensemble
blurb: Russian folk ensemble and contemporary composers in dialogue — Galician village songs meeting minimalist orchestration.
description: A recording by the Opus Posth Ensemble and the Dmitry Pokrovsky Folk Ensemble, performing a work by Russian composer Vladimir Martynov inspired by Slavic legends. It combines ancient calendar song melodies with minimalist structure and the opposition of acoustic folk voices against instruments.

blurb: The founding statement of Japanese ambient — Yoshimura's nature-inspired synth work remains one of the most perfect records of stillness.
description: Hiroshi Yoshimura's beloved 1986 ambient album, recorded at his home studio in Tokyo over the winter of 1985-86. Original copies became extremely rare and sought-after before a 2020 reissue on Light in the Attic.

blurb: Yoshimura designing sound for a resort hotel — light, airy, and surprisingly affecting in its studied calm.
description: A 1984 album by Hiroshi Yoshimura, originally commissioned by Shiseido as a promotional record for their AIR perfume line, released on white vinyl with a drop of the perfume inside. Side A evokes a forest with minimal synth and birdsong, side B evokes the sea with waves and gulls.

blurb: Kagayaki (radiance) lives up to its name — Masakatsu's delicate laptop-folk shimmering between human breath and digital light.
description: Takagi Masakatsu's 2014 album, recorded after he moved to a small village in Hyogo, Japan, blending piano with field recordings, village folk singing, and traditional Japanese music.

blurb: Japanese percussionist Midori Takada's 1983 masterpiece — solo marimba in ritual conversation with silence and resonance.
description: Japanese percussionist Midori Takada's 1983 solo debut, a four-part suite performed entirely on acoustic percussion instruments, marimba, reed organ, and piano, drawing on African and Asian rhythmic traditions. Recorded in two days in Tokyo and largely ignored until it went viral decades later.

blurb: Portuguese electronic music's best-kept secret — Canavarro's 1988 album prefiguring glitch, ambient, and microsound by decades.
description: A 1988 album by Portuguese musician Nuno Canavarro, made with only an 8-bit sampler and 8-track tape recorder, consisting of sparse electronically processed tones and treated spoken word. It circulated in near obscurity until a 1998 reissue brought it attention as a precursor to glitch and IDM.

blurb: Reich's landmark minimalist work — interlocking rhythms and slowly shifting harmonics creating one of music's most transcendent experiences.
description: Steve Reich's 1978 recording of his landmark minimalist composition, built across 11 sections over marimba, xylophone, vibraphone, clarinets, piano, strings, and voices. When it was released it was immediately influential, and has since been described as one of the works that altered the course of Western music.

blurb: Oldfield's most mystical suite — Celtic pipes, African percussion, and choral voices weaving together over two sides of pure atmosphere.
description: Mike Oldfield's third album from 1975, recorded at his home studio in Herefordshire, structured as two long pieces that move between Celtic folk and progressive rock. He played most of the instruments himself, including bouzouki, bodhran, harp, and synthesizers.

blurb: Hassell's Fourth World theory fully realised — tightly rhythmic and immersive, bridging gamelan, electronics, and global pulse.
description: Jon Hassell's 1986 album on ECM, his only release for the label, produced by Brian Eno and engineered by Daniel Lanois. It exemplifies Hassell's 'fourth world' approach, mixing his processed trumpet with ethno percussion in a tribal ambient style.

blurb: Jon Hassell meeting Burkinabe percussion ensemble Farafina — a document of genuine cross-cultural encounter, rhythmically irresistible.
description: A 1988 collaboration between American trumpeter Jon Hassell and Farafina, a group of Burkinabe musicians, produced by Brian Eno and Daniel Lanois. Farafina's dense West African polyrhythms share the album with Hassell's treated trumpet.

blurb: Warm synthesizer music made for plants — Garson's 1976 cult gem is tender, cosmic, and genuinely ahead of its time.
description: A 1976 Moog synthesizer record Mort Garson made specifically for plants, originally given away free with houseplant purchases at a Los Angeles garden store. It became a cult classic after Sacred Bones reissued it in 2019.

blurb: Steinbrick's ambient-classical hybrid navigating personal loss — unhurried and deeply felt, like water finding its own level.
description: LA-based multi-instrumentalist Josiah Steinbrick's 2017 debut solo album, built from nine improvised pieces using percussion, electronics, and tonal instruments. Produced by Cate Le Bon, it's slow-moving and minimal.

blurb: Percussionist Joe Westerlund (Megafaun) unfolding solo ambient pieces — patient, spatial, and full of quiet wonder.
description: Joe Westerlund's 2020 solo debut, centered on gongs, drones, and textured percussion. He recruited collaborators including Matt Douglas of the Mountain Goats to build something meditative and quietly intricate.

blurb: Tokyo percussion collective channelling Steve Reich and African drumming — kinetic, joyful minimalism from 1981.
description: A 1981 Japanese album from a group led by percussionist Midori Takada, mixing marimba, vibraphone, bamboo instruments, and synthesizers. It pulls from minimalism and African rhythmic traditions.

blurb: Russian ambient project constructing hazy, dream-state soundscapes — warm drones dissolving into ambient light.
description: A 2010 compilation of recordings by Pospulenn, a guitar-focused ambient project from Russia. Layered melodies and field recordings sit in a warm space between folk and ambient.

blurb: Essential compilation of Japanese fourth-world music 1980–86 — curious synthesizers, acoustic percussion, and an era's particular quiet optimism.
description: A 2010 DJ mix by Spencer Doran (of Visible Cloaks) collecting Japanese ambient and experimental pop from 1980 to 1986. Features Haruomi Hosono, Ryuichi Sakamoto, and the Mkwaju Ensemble among others.

blurb: Continued excavation of Japan's fertile fourth-world experiment — more forgotten gems from a golden era of spatial electronics.
description: The follow-up mix from Spencer Doran, continuing his survey of early 80s Japanese fourth world and ambient music. Sits in a similar space to the first volume, bridging kankyo ongaku, New Age, and Balearic sounds.

blurb: Brooklyn's Chanel Beads making indie pop strange again — layered vocals, nervous percussion, and hooks that dissolve into texture.
description: The 2024 debut album from New York-based musician Shane Lavers as Chanel Beads, released on Jagjaguwar. It weaves between soft acoustic indie pop, ambient pieces, and processed vocals.

blurb: Oslo-based DJ Sprinter threading bass, breakbeat, and UK-influenced club sounds through a distinctly Scandinavian sensibility.
description: A 2026 three-track release from Oslo-based DJ Sprinter, delivering breakbeat-driven cuts including a rework of Overmono's Daisy Chain.

blurb: Amsterdam electronic producer CRYME building intense, rhythmically complex club music.
description: A 2026 EP from Amsterdam producer CRYME on the Oddysee label, offering five club-focused tracks mixing deep house, dubby grooves, and rhythmic vocal elements.

blurb: New York's Fcukers making indie house with wit and weight — dance music that doesn't take itself too seriously while absolutely meaning it.
description: The 2026 debut album from New York duo Fcukers, released on Ninja Tune. Shanny Wise and Jackson Walker Lewis mix house, drum and bass, garage, and Y2K-era pop in a hyperactive club record produced by Kenny Beats with contributions from Dylan Brady of 100 Gecs.

blurb: Deeply atmospheric downtempo and trip-hop — patient, textured, and carried along on a gentle, persistent pulse.
description: A 2025 album released on the 3XL label, moving between downtempo, dub, dream pop, and trip-hop.

blurb: London project exploring post-new wave and experimental pop with emotional transparency — rough edges and genuine feeling.
description: A UK experimental and indie release from This Thing of Ours, blending lo-fi songwriting with atmospheric production.

blurb: Fractured breakbeat electronics — rhythms spliced and reconstituted into something post-everything yet viscerally immediate.
description: A 2025 release from psychoangel on Kitty on Fire Records, mixing hardcore breaks, jungle, and industrial electronics into 11 short tracks. Available on hand-dubbed cassette.

blurb: Brazilian solo project weaving black metal intensity through acoustic folk — Water Paths, a record about place and sound as landscape.
description: A 2026 album by Brazilian solo project Kaatayra, led by Caio Lemos, blending acoustic black metal with Amazonian folk, field recordings, and indigenous sounds. Written in memory of Lemos's grandmother.

blurb: Brian Transeau's trance masterwork — Ima balances programmatic intricacy with pure emotional uplift, a landmark of the mid-90s club era.
description: BT's 1995 debut, an early and influential progressive trance record on Perfecto Records. It featured the UK Dance Chart number one 'Embracing the Future' and a US version added 'Blue Skies' with Tori Amos.

blurb: Buckethead's most intimate record
description: A 1998 album Buckethead made for his mother while she was ill, stepping back from his usual guitar pyrotechnics for softer, atmospheric acoustic playing. Brain from Primus handled the drum programming.

blurb: German dub-techno duo navigating the space between abstraction and groove — precise, vaporous, and immersive.
description: The sole album by German duo Burger/Ink, released in 1996 on Harvest Records. Jörg Burger and Mike Ink combine dub and ambient textures into a slow, hypnotic minimal techno record out of Cologne.

blurb: C418 beyond Minecraft — Excursions is a proper ambient-electronic statement, refined and contemplative with unexpected emotional depth.
description: C418's 2018 album, a departure from his Minecraft ambient work into house, IDM, and electronic dance. Built entirely on a MacBook Pro, it runs over 100 minutes and was his first non-Minecraft release to get mainstream press coverage.

blurb: Indian-born, Canada-based Rupa's debut is a rare thing — Bollywood kitsch and cosmic disco meeting on a Toronto dancefloor, warm and delirious.
description: A rare 1982 album recorded in Calgary by Indian musician Rupa Biswas with a mix of Indian and Canadian studio musicians. It puts sarod and synthesizer against a disco beat, landing somewhere between Bollywood and Balearic. Reissued by Numero Group.

blurb: Intimate UK indie rock — Lewis threads honest lyricism through clean guitar arrangements, a record about the texture of everyday life.
description: Mark William Lewis's 2023 debut LP, recorded in his flat in Deptford, London. It mixes indie rock, dream pop, and experimental elements, with lyrics exploring life, death, and the weight of everyday experience.

blurb: A sharper, more propulsive follow-up — Pleasure Is Everything finds Lewis refining his songcraft, balancing urgency with restraint.
description: A 2024 vinyl compilation of Mark William Lewis's earlier EPs, released in a limited edition of 150. His music blends lo-fi indie rock with ambient and hypnagogic pop, drawing on his view of London from a tower block flat.

blurb: Early computer music with a human heart — Stone's sample-based compositions rewire pop and film music into something genuinely strange and new.
description: A 1992 electroacoustic album by LA composer Carl Stone, built from short looped samples of found music that shift and evolve using computer-processed windowing techniques. The pieces are named after restaurants.

blurb: A compilation of ambient IDM from one of the genre's quietest masters — deep, patient, and filled with warmth.
description: A 2004 double album collecting 29 previously unreleased tracks by Milwaukee's Erik Kowalski as Casino Versus Japan, originally given as a private gift. Dreamy IDM and downtempo with a gentle, ghostly quality.

blurb: The vaporwave landmark — 猫 シ Corp.'s 2014 record conjures an impossible nostalgia for places and times that never existed.
description: A 2014 vaporwave album by Dutch musician Cat System Corp., widely credited with helping establish the mallsoft subgenre. The title is a Welsh word for longing for a place you cannot return to.

blurb: Tokyo's cero channeling Afro-funk and contemporary pop into something unmistakably their own — polyrhythmic, sophisticated, alive.
description: Cero's 2018 album, a Tokyo band known for genre-mixing J-Pop. This record leans into nu-jazz, funk, and Shibuya-kei, with 12 tracks built around complex rhythms and horn-heavy arrangements.

blurb: Montreal producer Mike Silver building dream-pop structures from ambient and electronic parts — hazy, cinematic, softly euphoric.
description: A 2021 album by Montreal producer CFCF (Mike Silver), revisiting the sounds of late-90s techno, house, and IDM through a nostalgic lens. Blends elements of breakbeat, rock, and dance-pop into something that sounds like a childhood memory of the internet era.

blurb: New York duo at peak form — Something is clever synthpop with real emotional weight, Caroline Polachek's voice carrying the whole thing.
description: Chairlift's 2012 second album, the first with just Caroline Polachek and Patrick Wimberly after losing a founding member. Produced by Dan Carey, it sits in 80s-influenced synthpop with Polachek's sharp, high-register vocals at the center.

blurb: Japanese group fusing j-pop and hip hop with an irresistible lightness — group harmony meeting boom-bap in the most joyful way.
description: A 2019 future funk and electronic pop album by Chance de la Soul, released on the Business Casual label. Slick sampled loops, funk chops, and a light, summery feel throughout.

blurb: The second album that cemented big beat as a genre — harder, faster, and more viscerally exciting than almost anything of its era.
description: The Chemical Brothers' 1997 second album and one of the defining big beat records, featuring 'Block Rockin' Beats' and collaborations with Noel Gallagher and Mercury Rev. It hit number one in the UK and won a Grammy.

blurb: Merseyside new wave at its most sophisticated — lush production and genuine songwriting elevating the post-punk moment into something lasting.
description: China Crisis's second album from 1983, a new wave and synthpop record from Liverpool that added live brass and woodwind to their electronic sound. It spent 16 weeks on the UK Albums Chart.

blurb: Japanese-American duo making trip-hop about food, fantasy, and identity — irreverent, intoxicating, and still unlike anything else.
description: Cibo Matto's 1996 debut, made by New York-based Japanese duo Miho Hatori and Yuka Honda. Trip-hop beats and hip-hop-influenced collages back Hatori's rapping and singing, with lyrics frequently revolving around food.

blurb: UK progressive house in peak form — long, patient builds and elegant drops, the dancefloor as contemplative space.
description: Circulation's 2000 debut, compiling their early 12-inches into a double-disc set. Color-named tracks across deep house, tech house, and progressive house, clean and precise throughout.

blurb: Japanese shoegaze at its most maximal — Nobu Kajiwara burying melody under walls of distortion and synth wash, lovingly.
description: A 2007 album from Tokyo band Coaltar of the Deepers, who formed in 1991. It mixes shoegaze with heavy metal, techno, and ambient, and is considered a late-career culmination of their sound.

blurb: The moment Coil embraced acid house and broke everything open — strange, erotic, devotional, one of the great avant-garde dance records.
description: Coil's 1991 fourth album, where the UK experimental duo absorbed acid house into their dense, sample-heavy production. The album acronym LSD was intentional, and features guest vocals from Marc Almond.

blurb: Cécile Schott constructing music from melodica, loops, and silence — intimate, unhurried, made from found things.
description: Colleen's 2005 second album, from Paris-based artist Cécile Schott. She builds folk-influenced instrumental pieces using harpsichords, music boxes, and zithers, creating something quiet and slightly otherworldly.

blurb: Transgressive Portuguese pop from one of Europe's most confrontational performers — maximalist camp, Moorish influences, and genuine unease.
description: Portuguese artist Conan Osiris's 2017 debut, mixing dancehall, fado, funaná, hip-hop, metal, and eurodance into a chaotic and ambitious whole. Often compared to Björk for its experimental eclecticism.

blurb: UK bass music with genuine compositional ambition — Culprate's debut is dense with ideas, melodies that surface and vanish inside the rhythm.
description: Culprate's 2014 debut LP, crowd-funded and self-released, pulling together IDM, trip-hop, dubstep, and progressive rock influences. Eleven tracks with a broad and restless sonic range.

blurb: Baltimore's Dan Deacon at his most tender — communal maximalism giving way to something intimate, weird, and quietly moving.
description: Dan Deacon's 2020 fifth album on Domino, returning to maximal synth pop after a five-year gap. Made during a period of meditation and therapy, it's brighter and more personal than his earlier work.

blurb: Nicolas Jaar and Dave Harrington returning with something slower and stranger — cosmic Americana dissolving into electronic drift and back again.
description: Darkside's 2021 second album, Nicolas Jaar and Dave Harrington's first together since 2014. Recorded largely in a week-long session in New Jersey, it's a slow, psychedelic electronic record released on Matador.

blurb: The sound of digital utopia curdling — dds.wmilives crafting hypnagogic vaporwave from mall music and Windows audio, beautiful and unsettling.
description: A 2014 vaporwave album from death's dynamic shroud, blending ambient, psychedelic, and folktronica elements into their characteristically dream-like collage style.

blurb: Rod Modell's dub techno as pure environmental sound — Sommer is humidity, warmth, slow summer mornings, beats reduced to suggestion.
description: Rod Modell's 2012 Deepchord album on Soma Records, 13 tracks of dub techno built from modulating textures, shifting rhythms, and field recordings. Considered among his strongest solo work.

blurb: The collaboration that defined dark dub techno — Liumin is vast, patient, and completely absorbing from start to finish.
description: A collaboration between Rod Modell and Steve Hitchell as Deepchord Presents Echospace, released around 2010. Deeply immersive dub techno drawing on field recordings from Tokyo, with a heavy, slowly shifting low-end.

artist: desert sand feels warm at night
blurb: Chinese vaporwave from one of the movement's most thoughtful practitioners — found sounds and digital longing stitched into something genuinely moving.
description: A 2021 vaporwave album from UK artist desert sand feels warm at night, stretching sampled 80s and 90s pop into slow, dreamy ambient loops for over an hour.

blurb: Breakbeat with an eye on the floor and an ear for chaos — UK club music that doesn't apologise for itself.
description: DJ CAMGIRL's 2016 debut album, a juke and footwork-rooted record mixing acid, chopped electronics, and club structures. Reissued on vinyl in 2021 by Doom Trip Records.

blurb: Benny Rodrigues's tribute to the rave era — trance loops stretched into something devotional, a record that still sounds like the future.
description: A 2020 four-LP trance album from Traumprinz under the DJ Metatron alias, released on All Possible Worlds. A tribute to 90s rave culture, mixing euphoric trance with ambient passages.

blurb: The footwork album that introduced Chicago's mutant dance music to the world — Rashad's Double Cup is both technically astonishing and emotionally devastating.
description: DJ Rashad's only full-length album, released on Hyperdub in 2013 and finished just before his death in 2014. It brought Chicago footwork to a global audience and is credited with popularizing the genre internationally.

blurb: Terre Thaemlitz mapping the geography of New York's queer underground — deep house as political statement, slow, uncompromising, essential.
description: Terre Thaemlitz's 2009 album as DJ Sprinkles, a deep house record built as a critique of how the genre's queer and marginal origins got erased by mainstream culture. Resident Advisor named it their album of the year.

blurb: Jimmy Tamborello's bedroom electronic landmark — tender, low-key, and full of the kind of beauty that doesn't announce itself.
description: Dntel's 2001 debut on Sub Pop, a delicate IDM and indietronica record from LA producer Jimmy Tamborello. Best known for the track '(This Is) The Dream of Evan and Chan' featuring Ben Gibbard, which directly led to The Postal Service.

blurb: Roman techno producer interpreting Chris Madak's compositions — dark, meditative ambient techno where time genuinely stops.
description: Italian techno producer Donato Dozzy reworking material from Philadelphia ambient musician Bee Mask (Chris Madak), recorded after the two met at Japan's Labyrinth festival in 2012. Seven ambient reimaginings of a single source track, released in 2013 on Spectrum Spools.

blurb: Percussion and electronics at the edge of the listenable — Stadium is Keszler at his most architectural, building structures from sound.
description: Eli Keszler's 2018 album on Shelter Press, made after his move from Brooklyn to Manhattan. Avant-garde percussion alongside Rhodes chords, woodwind, and field recordings, complex but grounded.

id: Love in the Time of Science
blurb: Icelandic pop at its most exquisite — Torrini's debut has trip-hop production and a voice that sounds like it fell from somewhere high.
description: Icelandic singer Emilíana Torrini's 1999 international debut, produced by Roland Orzabal of Tears for Fears. Trip-hop beats and downtempo arrangements behind her folk-influenced voice.

blurb: Lo-fi indie rock from one of the underground's most committed voices — Western Teleport is both sonically frail and emotionally immense.
description: Emperor X's 2011 album on Bar/None, made by former science teacher Chad Matheny. Lo-fi indie pop with folk and electronic touches, with lyrics that contrast personal life against large political and environmental forces.

blurb: Danish-Portuguese R&B with a cool, considered touch — de Casier's debut is understated and precise, pop that doesn't flinch from its own intelligence.
description: Erika de Casier's 2019 self-released debut, from the Portuguese-born Danish singer and producer. Cool, minimal R&B drawing on 90s and early 2000s G-funk, bossa nova, and trip-hop.

blurb: Chicago DJ and cosmic connector — Quivering in Time is devotional house music, a record made for the body and the spirit at once.
description: Chicago-born DJ and producer Eris Drew's 2021 debut album on her own T4T LUV NRG label, recorded in a log cabin in rural New Hampshire. Nine house tracks that flow together like a DJ set, built around a spiritual connection to the dancefloor.

Nitin Sawhney's 1999 album on Outcaste Records, blending drum and bass, jazz, Indian classical music, and hip-hop. Conceptually structured around nuclear weapons and runs backward from the India-Pakistan tests to Robert Oppenheimer quoting the Bhagavad Gita.
